## Recommended hypothesis (final wording)

> **Social psychology — the `Social` discipline, i.e. the social/personality-psychology domain that consists mainly of the Reproducibility Project: Psychology (RPP) original/replication pairs plus the social-psychology effects of Many Labs 1 and 3 — is the domain in which both the original and the replication studies relied primarily on student subjects.** In these 74 social-psychology O/R pairs the student share is high on **both** sides of every replication (original 62/73 = 84.9%, replication 60/73 = 82.2% at study level; 83.6%/80.6% when the four repeated titles are collapsed; 82.2%/78.6% over all lab-level rows), which brackets the quoted pair (82.4%, 80.9%). By contrast cognitive psychology never pairs a near-82% original share with a near-81% replication share (75.5% original vs 81.6% replication), and experimental economics is essentially saturated at student samples (94.4% → 100%). The pattern is a *social-psychology* pattern: a domain whose original studies were already ~82–85% student samples and whose replications stayed at ~78–82% students, with the small drop driven by replications switching to online/community/anyone samples — note that `online` appears only as a replication subject type (0 originals vs 148 replication rows), so part of the drop is a sampling-mode shift, not a change of target population.

## Headline table (n=141 O/R pairs; aggregated roll-up for ml1/ml3; denominator = non-missing coding)

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| project | rpp | 97 | 78/96 | 81.25 | 74/96 | 77.08 | 1.15 | 3.82 | 4.97 |
| journal-derived field | Social/personality psychology | 84 | 66/83 | 79.52 | 64/83 | 77.11 | 2.88 | 3.79 | 6.67 |
| discipline | Cognitive | 49 | 37/49 | 75.51 | 40/49 | 81.63 | 6.89 | 0.73 | 7.62 |
| journal-derived field | Cognitive psychology | 30 | 27/30 | 90.00 | 27/30 | 90.00 | 7.60 | 9.10 | 16.70 |
| project | ml1 | 16 | 12/16 | 75.00 | 16/16 | 100.00 | 7.40 | 19.10 | 26.50 |
| project | ml3 | 10 | 9/10 | 90.00 | 10/10 | 100.00 | 7.60 | 19.10 | 26.70 |
| discipline / project / field | Economics / ee / Economics | 18 | 17/18 | 94.44 | 18/18 | 100.00 | 12.04 | 19.10 | 31.14 |

| journal-derived field | Judgment & decision making | 1 | 1/1 | 100.00 | 1/1 | 100.00 | 17.6 | 19.1 | 36.70 |

| journal-derived field | Political science / public opinion | 3 | 0/3 | 0.00 | 3/3 | 100.00 | 82.4 | 19.1 | 101.50 |

Ranked candidates (min dev_total across 7 conventions): **Social 1.49 → rpp 2.94 → Cognitive 7.62 → ml1 26.5 → ml3 26.7 → Economics/ee 31.1**.

## Sensitivity (pct_o / pct_r per convention)
| convention | Social | rpp | Cognitive |
|---|---|---|---|
| **headline** (141 studies, missing excluded) | 84.93 / 82.19 | 81.25 / 77.08 | 75.51 / 81.63 |
| missing counted as non-student | 83.78 / 81.08 | 80.41 / 76.29 | 75.51 / 81.63 |
| unique `title` dedup (135) | 83.58 / 80.60 | 80.85 / 76.60 | 75.51 / 81.63 |
| lab-row level (927 rows) | 82.16 / 78.56 | 81.25 / 77.08 | 71.37 / 83.82 |
| lab rows excl. aggregated (901) | 82.10 / 77.93 | 81.25 / 77.08 | 71.37 / 83.33 |
| modal lab-row subject code | 84.93 / 82.19 | 81.25 / 77.08 | 75.51 / 81.63 |
| `drop==True` excluded (131) | 93.75 / 85.94 | 84.44 / 80.00 | 75.51 / 81.63 |

**Social wins in 6 of the 7 conventions** (rpp wins only when `drop==True` studies are removed — and there Social itself moves to 93.75/85.94 and stops matching the target at all).

## No exact reproduction — reported as a finding, not fixed by post-hoc grouping
An exhaustive 1–2-column grouping search (17 fields × 4 row bases, min group size 8 → **3,251 candidate categories**) found the smallest deviations for **non-domain artefacts**: `online.o==0 & same_country==1` at lab level (82.64/80.75, dev 0.38), `drop==False & same_country==0` (81.94/80.83), `experiment_language.o=='English' & same_language==1` (83.15/80.90). These are procedural intersections, not domains, so they do not answer the question. **No `project`, `discipline`, or journal-derived field reproduces 82.4/80.9 exactly**; the closest domain is Social (dev 1.49 at best, 3.82 in the headline). The source table must have used an undocumented convention — most plausibly a title-deduplicated or missing-as-non-student study-level cut of the Social discipline, which yields 83.58/80.60 or 83.78/81.08, within ~1 pp of the quoted pair.

## Within-domain detail (Social, n=74)
* `subjects.o`: students 62, anyone 7, community 4, missing 1. `subjects.r`: students 60, anyone 6, online 4, community 3, missing 1.
* o→r transitions: students→students 56; students→online 3 (rpp.43, rpp.49, rpp.68); students→anyone 2; students→community 1; anyone→students 2; anyone→anyone 4; anyone→online 1; community→students 2; community→community 2; missing 1.
* Non-student originals are all `anyone`/`community`: ml1.9/.10/.11 (public-opinion/survey studies, all `drop==True`) and rpp.46/.56/.59/.73/.77/.93/.97/.114 (+ missing rpp.154).
* Runner-up rpp (n=97): o students 78 / anyone 10 / community 8 / missing 1; r students 74 / anyone 9 / community 9 / online 4 / missing 1.

## Limitations
1. **File B excluded.** `..._replication_success_data_...csv` (143×15) has no subject column and no key to File A (0/143 exact `study==authors.o`; 83/143 recoverable by surname overlap; 0/31 Experimental Philosophy studies exist in File A), so any answer phrased in its "Psychology / Social Sciences / Experimental Philosophy / Experimental Economics" vocabulary cannot be computed from the staged data; the closest computable analogue is still the psychology/social-psychology set.
2. `subjects.o` is constant within `id`; `subjects.r` varies within the 16 ml1 ids, so the aggregated-roll-up choice matters for ml1 only (study-level 100% vs lab-level 73.0% replication students).
3. 1 study (rpp.154) lacks subject coding; 4 titles are repeated across ids (135 unique titles / 141 ids).
4. Percentages are unweighted study counts — no effect-size, sample-size, or lab-count weighting.
5. Because the target pair is not reproduced exactly, the deliverable is an identification of the best-fitting domain, not a verification of the source table's exact arithmetic.

payload.hypothesis: Social psychology (the `Social` discipline — the social/personality-psychology domain dominated by the Reproducibility Project: Psychology pairs, plus the social-psychology effects of Many Labs 1 and 3) is the domain in which both the original and the replication studies primarily used student subjects. In these 74 O/R pairs 62/73 = 84.9% of originals and 60/73 = 82.2% of replications used student subjects at the study level (83.6%/80.6% when the four repeated titles are collapsed, 82.2%/78.6% across all lab-level rows), a pair that brackets the quoted 82.4%/80.9% and is the closest match of any domain under 6 of the 7 analytic conventions tested. Cognitive psychology (75.5% original vs 81.6% replication) and experimental economics (94.4% vs 100%) fail to show the same near-82%/near-81% combination. Within Social the only departure from student samples is on the replication side (3 studies moved from student to online samples, plus anyone/community samples), and the `online` subject type exists only in replications (0 originals vs 148 replication rows), so the original-to-replication decline reflects a shift in sampling mode rather than in the target population.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded both staged CSVs (File A 927x57 with 141 unique O/R ids; File B 143x15). 2) Join diagnostics showed File B has no subject column and no usable key (0/143 exact study==authors.o, 83/143 surname matches, 0/31 Experimental Philosophy studies in File A), so File B was excluded and the limitation reported. 3) Built the headline study-level frame: the 26 aggregated==True roll-up rows (ml1/ml3) + the 115 non-aggregated rpp/ee rows = 141 unique ids, asserted. 4) Derived a robustness `field` variable from `journal`/title (social-personality, cognitive, economics, political science/public opinion, Psych Science, judgment & decision, general science). 5) For every candidate category computed n studies, students.o n/%, students.r n/% over denominator = non-missing subject coding, plus deviation |pct_o-82.4|+|pct_r-80.9|; ranked discipline, project and journal-derived field in one table. 6) Re-ran the same statistics under 7 conventions (headline; missing-as-non-student; unique-title dedup; lab-row level 927; lab rows excluding aggregated; modal lab-row subject code; drop==True excluded) and recorded each category's range and best deviation. 7) Ran an exhaustive 1-2-column grouping search (17 fields x 4 row bases, min group size 8, 3251 candidate categories) to test whether any category reproduces 82.4/80.9; the closest hits were non-domain procedural intersections, reported as evidence that the source table used an undocumented convention rather than used as the answer. 8) Inspected within-category detail for Social and for runner-up rpp (subject-type distributions, o->r transitions, list of non-student studies, online-only-in-replications fact). 9) Wrote out/headline_categories.csv, out/sensitivity_table.csv, out/exhaustive_grouping_search.csv, out/social_discipline_studies.csv, out/analysis_log.txt and out/REPORT.md.
